brief.headline: Move from 100% advance to 30-day credit and match the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹66.48/KG — the price we already pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose
priceAsk.basis: We're paying ₹70.80/KG to Sukhjit but only ₹66.48/KG to Sayaji for identical material — a 6.5% gap. The open market asks ₹60–81/kg (typically ₹66–73), so ₹66.48 sits right in the fair band. Hold them to the lowest price we already pay.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Switch from 100% advance to normal 30-day credit after delivery
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's locked in advance payments right now

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit is big — ₹1555.82 Cr in sales — and growing fast at 29.7% a year, so they want new orders. But they keep only 2.9% of every ₹100 they sell as profit, meaning margins are razor-thin and a steep price cut could squeeze them hard. We're tiny to them: our ₹1.06 Cr is just 0.07% of their revenue, so alone we have almost no pull. Their overall health score is D (44/100), signalling moderate stress. The play: bundle the price ask with a volume commitment (tie more SKUs or longer contract), push hardest on the advance-payment term (it costs them nothing and unlocks real cash for us), and keep Sayaji and the other alternates visible so they know this isn't their business by default.

evidence.point: We pay Sukhjit 6.5% more than the best price we already have
evidence.figure: ₹70.80/KG vs ₹66.48/KG; gap 6.5%; costs us an extra ₹12.95 L a year

evidence.point: We are a very small customer to them
evidence.figure: ₹1.06 Cr spend = 0.07% of their ₹1555.82 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They are growing sales fast and will want to keep volume
Paying 100% in advance locks up our cash; moving to 30 days frees up real money
Open-market asking price sits in the same range as our target

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited (current supplier)
alternates.why: Already delivers Dextrose to us at ₹66.48/KG — our benchmark and proof the price is real

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B (62/100) — a drop-in alternate to Sayaji and Sukhjit

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹821.13 Cr revenue, growing capacity — another credible second source

risks: At 0.07% of their sales we have almost no individual leverage — they can easily walk away unless we bundle more volume or a longer commit.
Their 2.9% profit margin leaves little room: push the price too hard without a volume sweetener and they may cut quality or service to protect margin.
Health score D (44/100) signals moderate financial stress — if we squeeze and they stumble, our supply is at risk; keep a qualified alternate warm.
We're paying 100% advance today, so they're used to zero credit risk from us — they will resist any payment term that shifts risk back to them; lead with how fast we pay and our credit strength.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to keep growing with you, but right now we're paying you ₹70.80 when Sayaji delivers the same Dextrose at ₹66.48 — and we're paying 100% up front, which locks up nearly ₹9 lakh of our cash.
